name: Bharti Airtel Ltd
about: Bharti Airtel Ltd is one of the world’s leading providers of telecommunication services with presence in 18 countries representing India, Sri Lanka, 14 countries in Africa. [1]

business.what: Bharti Airtel is a telecom group whose India business sells mobile, home broadband (fibre and FWA), digital TV and B2B connectivity and cloud/data-centre services, and whose Africa business runs mobile, money and data services. Revenue comes mainly from subscriber usage, plans and enterprise contracts.

segments.name: India Mobile
segments.comment: Q1 ARPU Rs.264 with 3.3M revenue-earning customer adds; ARPU lifted partly by an extra day.

segments.name: Homes (fibre and FWA broadband)
segments.comment: Net adds of 473,000, a moderation as FWA acquisition quality was tightened.

segments.name: Digital TV
segments.comment: Added 6,000 customers, led by IPTV adoption.

segments.name: Airtel Business (B2B)
segments.comment: Revenue about Rs.5,670 Cr, up 3.2% QoQ and nearly 12% YoY on large deal wins.

segments.name: Africa
segments.comment: Constant-currency revenue growth of 5.7%; contributed almost half of group revenue growth.

segments.name: Airtel Money / Payments Bank and Finance
segments.comment: Payments bank run-rate over Rs.3,400 Cr; NBFC lending went live this quarter.

ledger.promise: Reach over 1 GW data centre operating capacity (later firmed to 3-4 years)
ledger.quote: The partnership with Google, coupled with the ongoing expansion in Nxtra, gives us a clear visibility to get to over 1 gigawatt in the next few years.
ledger.actual: Calls cite 120-150 MW (Feb 2026), then 120-130 MW (Aug 2026). Q1 FY27 identifies only 'a couple of hundred' MW under build over two years.

ledger.promise: About 25% data centre market share at 1 GW, up from about 12%
ledger.quote: in the next three to four years, we will have about a gigawatt capacity, which will give us about 25% share
ledger.actual: Deadline is Feb 2029-30. No later call updates the market share figure.

ledger.promise: Capex to hold or decline on an annualised basis and moderate over time
ledger.quote: At an annualized basis, like we have guided, directionally, there is a holding/decline in capex.
ledger.actual: Cash used in investing fell from 60,198 (FY25) to 56,205 (FY26), down 3,993 or 6.6%. Capital WIP rose from 10,999 to 12,938.

ledger.promise: FY27 capex in the ballpark of FY26, give or take a little
ledger.quote: our sense is that we will be in the ballpark of this year, give or take a little bit
ledger.actual: No full-year FY27 cash flow yet. Capital WIP stands at 13,607 against 12,938 at FY26.

ledger.promise: Further reduction in debt going forward
ledger.quote: there is reduction and you will see reduction going forth
ledger.actual: Borrowings fell from 213,642 (FY25) to 195,412 (FY26), then rose to 199,432 in the latest FY27 figure (+4,020). Q1 FY27 says Nxtra will lever up.

ledger.promise: Some margin pressure from digital mix; margins to stay in the current ballpark, maybe slightly lower
ledger.quote: if we have to step up growth, there will be some margin pressures because there is just a mix of the business
ledger.actual: EBITDA margin was 56.9% in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, then 57.4% in Q2 FY27. It stayed in the ballpark; the expected pressure has not shown up.

ledger.promise: Sustained ARPU growth of 4-5% or slightly higher (earlier: headroom for many quarters)
ledger.quote: those levers, still, give us good headroom for continuing ARPU growth for many quarters to come
ledger.actual: No ARPU data. Consolidated revenue grew 16.7% YoY in Q2 FY27 (60,878 vs 52,145).

ledger.promise: Underlying enterprise growth of about 10% to show in coming quarters
ledger.quote: the underlying business is growing at 10%, which should show up in coming quarters if we do well
ledger.actual: No segment revenue in the materials, and no later call reports enterprise growth.

ledger.promise: Make 5G dual-mode (SA) commercial in the coming months
ledger.quote: we plan to make it commercial in the coming months as the traffic on our 5G network grows
ledger.actual: No later call reports a commercial launch.

ledger.promise: Build 56 edge data centres in 18-24 months
ledger.quote: we are focused right now on building in the next 18 to 24 months - 56 world class edge data centers
ledger.actual: Deadline is Nov 2027 to May 2028. The materials give no progress count.

ledger.promise: Airtel Money London listing in H2 2026
ledger.quote: Airtel Money is now preparing for a London listing in the second half of 2026.
ledger.actual: Deadline is Dec 2026. The materials have no confirmation of a listing as of 10 Nov 2026.

ledger.promise: Higher customer additions in H2 FY27; market back to old growth rates within two quarters
ledger.quote: We see a higher trend of customer additions towards the second half of the year
ledger.actual: H2 FY27 has not been reported. The materials have no subscriber data.

current_guidance.quote: we will continue to rapidly sort of scale up our data center portfolio as we are building out from the 120 to 130 megawatts, all the way to 1 gigawatt over the next few years.
The third is upcoming build that is already well underway and that will be a couple of hundred megawatts over the course of the next couple of years

current_guidance.target: Current ballpark, maybe trending slightly down
current_guidance.quote: I think, longer term, as the portfolio retools, we think the margins will be in this ballpark, maybe sort of trend slightly downwards
in the next five to seven years you will see sustained growth, just on account of ARPU as India gets more affluent, etc., of 4% or 5%, maybe slightly higher.

current_guidance.target: FY27 in the ballpark of FY26, give or take
current_guidance.quote: our sense is that we will be in the ballpark of this year, give or take a little bit

current_guidance.target: Nxtra to raise debt and lever up
current_guidance.quote: Nxtra will need to lever up in order to build out what is required over the next few years.

current_guidance.target: Higher additions in H2; market back to old growth rates
current_guidance.quote: hopefully in next quarter and the quarter after, everybody should be growing at old rates.

credibility.label: mixed
credibility.summary: Few promises can be settled from these materials: capex moderation held in FY26 (cash used in investing down 6.6%) and margins stayed where management said they would, but borrowings have risen 4,020 crore since the Q4 FY26 debt-reduction pledge. The main valuation promise, 1 GW of data centre capacity, shows no visible progress in the call figures (120-150 MW in Feb 2026, 120-130 MW in Aug 2026), and the ARPU, enterprise, 5G SA and fibre-rollout claims cannot be checked against reported numbers.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Capex would be elevated in the near future because Nxtra and the 5G/homes build were running in parallel.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Cash used in investing fell from 60,198 in FY25 to 56,205 in FY26 (-6.6%). Capital WIP rose only 1,939, to 12,938.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Stepping up growth in the digital businesses would bring some margin pressure from business mix.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: EBITDA margin went 56.9% (Q4 FY26) to 56.9% (Q1 FY27) to 57.4% (Q2 FY27). TTM margin is about 57.1%. No pressure is visible yet.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Debt reduction would continue going forward.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Borrowings went from 195,412 (FY26) to 199,432 (latest FY27), up 4,020 or 2.1%. One call later, management said Nxtra will need to lever up.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Data centre portfolio is being scaled up rapidly toward 1 GW.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Capacity cited on the calls went from 120-150 MW (Q3 FY26) to 120-130 MW (Q1 FY27). The build named in Q1 FY27 is a couple of hundred MW over two years. That is well short of the roughly 870 MW still needed for 1 GW by about 2029-30.

bull.point: Growth in revenue and profit remains strong.
Margins held despite management warning of mix pressure.
bull.evidence: EBITDA margin rose to 57.4% in Q2 FY27, up from 56.7% in Q2 FY26 and the highest in the series.

bull.point: Cash generation comfortably covers capex, and the capex discipline promise was kept in FY26.
bull.evidence: FY26 cash from operations was 122,230 against 56,205 used in investing, leaving about 66,025. Borrowings fell 18,230 in FY26. Debt is about 1.5x TTM EBITDA (199,432 / 130,523).

bear.point: Debt reduction has reversed and new leverage is planned.
bear.evidence: Borrowings rose from 195,412 to 199,432 after the Q4 FY26 promise of continued reduction. Q1 FY27 says Nxtra will need to lever up for its build-out.
bear.source: Q4 FY26 call p12; Q1 FY27 call p8; reported numbers

bear.point: The 1 GW data centre target lacks a visible path, and its timeline wording has loosened.
bear.evidence: Q3 FY26 said '3-4 years'; later calls say 'next few years'. Cited capacity is 120-130 MW, and only a couple of hundred MW are under build over two years.
bear.source: Q3 FY26 call p5; Q1 FY27 call p7, p9

bear.point: Customer and home-broadband momentum has softened, and much of the growth story cannot be verified here.
bear.evidence: Q1 FY27 cites an FWA pullback, slower home broadband contribution and recovery 'hopefully' within two quarters. ARPU, enterprise and subscriber claims have no supporting data in these materials.
bear.source: Q1 FY27 call p8, p15, p16
